newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran to hold run-offs for nine parliament seats.
newsitem.headline: Iran to hold run-offs for nine parliament seats.

text.p: Run-off polls will be needed in Iran to fill nine parliamentary seats left vacant after by-elections last week, newspapers said on Tuesday.

The newspapers said only 13 of the 22 seats contested in the Friday by-elections were filled by candidates who received the required one third of all votes cast in their districts and the remaining seats would be decided in run-off polls.
The results showed victory for five centrists, one candidate from a radical faction close to the centrists, and three conservatives, according to the factions' published list of candidates.
The other four winners had unknown affiliations or were independents. No date has been set for the run-off polls.
Three women were among the victors, bringing to 13 the number of female deputies in the 270-member assembly.

The results did not appear to affect the balance of power in the Majlis (parliament) where the conservatives, led by speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri, kept their majority in the main elections last year.
They face a strong minority coalition of centrist backers of President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, radical Islamist intellectuals and labour groups.

The by-elections were held to fill seats left empty after results of parliamentary polls in Iran's third largest city Isfahan and some other districts were annulled by the Guardian Council, a body of clerics and lawyers that oversees elections, because of alleged irregularities.
Local issues dominated the by-election campaigns, but there was tension between conservatives and centrists over a screening process which decided who was allowed to run.
The council screens candidates for their belief in Islam and Iran's system of Islamic government, including the rule that the state is headed by a supreme spiritual leader.
